value="<font style="font-size: 12px;"><b>How it Works</b></font><div><ul style="padding-left: 20px; margin-top: 5px;"><li><span style="font-size: 12px;">The semantic model provides the active Financial Entity population and associated hierarchy attributes to Excel using a DAX query over OLE DB.</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 12px;">Users classify each Financial Entity at an appropriate aggregation grain, with the selected hierarchy value automatically converted into a proposed modelling case.</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 12px;">Where required, a controlled override allows bespoke portfolio groupings.</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 12px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(51, 51, 51), rgb(193, 193, 193));">The workbook provides immediate feedback on the number of Financial Entities, resulting modelling cases, overrides and aggregation methods used.</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 12px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(51, 51, 51), rgb(193, 193, 193));">The completed mapping is then re-ingested through Power Query and joined back to the financial profile dataset using Financial Entity Key.</span></li></ul></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="343.21" width="350" x="473" y="119.79000000000002" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="51" connectable="0" parent="2" style="group" to modelling cases</span></li><li data-section-id="13gqmb9" data-start="793" data-end="901"><span style="font-size: 11px;"><b>Source traceability: </b>modelling cases remain traceable to originating div.div: Controlled Financial Entity to Modelling Case Translation

div.span: The Financial Entity to Modelling Case translation decouples source-system grain from modelling grain, allowing the semantic model to retain detailed Financial Entity data while the Scenario Modeller operates on a user-defined case-level structure.

li.span: The semantic model provides the active Financial Entity population and associated hierarchy attributes to Excel using a DAX query over OLE DB.
Users classify each Financial Entity at an appropriate aggregation grain, with the selected hierarchy value automatically converted into a proposed modelling case.
Where required, a controlled override allows bespoke portfolio groupings.

span.style: font-size: 12px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(51, 51, 51), rgb(193, 193, 193));

li.span: The workbook provides immediate feedback on the number of Financial Entities, resulting modelling cases, overrides and aggregation methods used.

span.style: font-size: 12px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(51, 51, 51), rgb(193, 193, 193));

li.span: The completed mapping is then re-ingested through Power Query and joined back to the financial profile dataset using Financial Entity Key.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

li.span: Controlled translation: defined rules map Financial Entities to modelling cases
Source traceability: modelling cases remain traceable to originating Financial Entities
Human accountability: users explicitly define and review case mappings
Complete population: validation identifies unmapped or incomplete entity assignments

li.span: Consistent classification: standard attributes support repeatable case construction
Stable identity: Financial Entity keys preserve identity through translation
Transparent overrides: user-defined grouping and naming remain explicit and reviewable
Separation of concerns: source hierarchy is preserved independently of modelling structure
